stories.title: Cabinet body discusses findings of Mir Raza judicial commission
summary: KARACHI: A cabinet subcommittee formed to oversee the implementation of the report of a judicial commission regarding the death of Mir Raza Ali met here to discuss the findings and a mechanism for their implementation.
The judicial commission’s report, which was made public by the provincial government on Tuesday, recommended, among other things, formation of a joint investigation team to probe the case.

According to a press release, the sub-committee reviewed matters relating to the implementation of the report and decided to submit its recommendations to the Sindh chief minister as soon as possible.

stories.title: What makes desperate families adopt suicide as ‘escape’?
summary: When mental health experts were asked to address this troubling question of how someone could persuade their spouse to participate in such an extreme act, they explained the psychiatric and psychological conditions that could lead up to such acts.

Responding to Dawn queries on the telephone, the CEO of Pakistan Institute of Mental Health, Rawalpindi, explained biological, psychological and social factors behind such suicides. “The issue spans biological, psychological, and social dimensions,” Dr Zubair said.

Alternatively, one person’s mental illness may cause significant stress for the other family members, creating a shared psychological impact, added the managing director of the Karachi Psychiatric Hospital. “The dominant personality in a family can also influence others.

stories.title: Talking taxes
summary: The priorities that have shaped Pakistan’s tax system over the years differ from what tax experts suggest it should serve.
One thing that is sorely needed in Pakistan is a more robust, mandatory data release template for the FBR, with monthly frequency at the very least, if not more often.

The government should legislate this requirement and make any necessary modifications to FBR rules to ensure that a dedicated team is always at work within the tax authority, gathering, compiling, and preparing the next data release as per a predetermined schedule.

stories.title: Spurring economic growth
summary: Pakistan already has a climate budget — the one written after each disaster.

Each district needs a short climate investment and growth plan that converts national targets into local units: acres under laser levelling and drip irrigation, tube-wells solarised, kilometres of drains cleared.
Local growth stays dependent on donor projects because no district or municipal body can borrow or issue a municipal bond.

stories.title: Makkah pact clarity
summary: THERE had been much speculation about what exactly the trilateral Makkah Joint Defence Agreement entails, other than general commitments about the collective defence of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye.

While the defence of Saudi Arabia is important, Pakistan, Turkiye, and other regional states should continue efforts to find a negotiated solution to the Yemen conflict — both between the Saudis and Houthis and within Yemen.
In a related development, Pakistan’s chief of defence forces was in Tehran on Tuesday to try and prevent further escalation on the war front.

stories.title: Maldives president, CDF Munir stress importance of strengthening defence cooperation
summary: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu underscored the importance of strengthening bilateral defence cooperation on Wednesday, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.

20 MoUs signed Pakistan and the Maldives signed a series of MoUs aimed at deepening bilateral relations in multiple sectors, including defence, IT, cybersecurity, health, education, social protection, agriculture and tourism, among others.
Muizzu, speaking to Dar, “expressed Maldives’ desire to deepen its close relations with Pakistan and explore new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation”, the FO said.

stories.title: Balochistan assembly panel okays whistleblower protection bill
summary: QUETTA: A provincial assembly committee on Wednesday advanced the Balochistan Whistleblower Protection Bill 2026 for final approval, bringing the proposed law designed to shield citizens who expose government corruption and administrative misconduct one step closer to enactment.

The Standing Committee on Services and General Administration Department (S&GAD) conducted a detailed and clause-by-clause review of the bill before recommending its submission to the house for approval.

The legislation aims to provide legal protection to individuals who disclose information in the public interest regarding corruption, abuse of authority and administrative irregularities in government affairs.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court seeks evidence against NAB officials’ appointments
summary: Chaudhry, observed that the petitioner had “completely ruined the entire case” after he argued that Mr Nasir had improperly described himself as a former judge despite having served only as an additional judge of the Lahore High Court (LHC).
The petitioner contended that Mr Shah had previously served as NAB prosecutor general, a position that did not qualify him as a federal government officer in Grade 21 or its equivalent.

Regarding Mr Nasir, the petitioner argued that he did not meet the criteria under Section 8(a) of the NAO, which requires a NAB prosecutor general to be qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.

stories.title: Kharmang celebrates colour, taste and aroma of Suspolo apples
summary: GILGIT: The vibrant colours, sweet taste and captivating aroma of indigenous Suspolo apples took centre stage at the 7th National Suspolo Festival 2026, held in Pari Valley of Kharmang district, celebrating the region’s unique agricultural heritage and hardworking farmers.

Organised by the district administration with the support of the Gilgit-Baltistan Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries Department, the festival brought together Governor Mehdi Shah, Forests Minister Raja Nasir Ali Khan, locals and domestic and foreign tourists.

Speaking to Dawn, Deputy Commissioner Kharmang Nisar Ahmed Khan said the annual festival, held during the harvest season for the past seven years, aims to promote the indigenous apple, showcase local culture and help farmers find better markets for their produce.

stories.title: ‘Letting roots of Pak-India conflict fester invites more danger’
summary: Gen Hayat warned that repeated crises between the nuclear-armed neighbours could become increasingly dangerous if unresolved disputes, diminishing restraint and the absence of sustained political dialogue continued to undermine regional security.

He said South Asia lacked an inclusive regional security framework, effective crisis-management mechanisms and sustained political dialogue. “The region lives between deterrence that prevents the worst and disputes that repeatedly regenerate danger,” he said.

Gen Hayat warned unverified allegations could trigger conflict before the facts were established, with a future confrontation potentially arising from an accident rather than a deliberate state decision.

stories.title: Saudis intercept more drones as conflict with Houthis spirals
summary: The Houthis denied having targeted the kingdom, with military spokesman Yahya Saree saying their forces had not carried out any “deep” operations in Saudi territory.

Egypt to support Saudis Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo’s proposed military support for Riyadh was to “defend Saudi territory, and does not include an attack on Yemen,” state-linked media reported.
Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

stories.title: PTI leadership ‘turns on itself’ after protest debacle
summary: The bad blood became public on Wednesday as two senior party leaders — Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and former KP chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur — traded accusations of betraying the party cause.

This prompted the secretary general to take a dig at “the narrative” regarding a possible announcement by a group of party MPAs, nominating a new provincial president without permission from their jailed leader Imran Khan, or the party’s political committee.

Ali Amin Gandapur The secretary general accused the group of cutting off contact with Sohail Afridi and his team in the final days of the protest march, paving the way for state coercion, emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

summary: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia on Wednesday signed a multilateral pact to promote cooperation in defence production and capabilities, the Turkish defence ministry said.

summary: According to Topline Securities, the new draft maintains the 1pc general sales tax (GST) rate on battery electric vehicles (BEVs), while setting rates at 9pc for plug-in hybrid vehicles (PHEVs) and 6pc for range-extended electric vehicles (REEVs).
Preliminary industry estimates suggest conventional petrol vehicles could become approximately 8-10pc cheaper, while hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) may see reductions of around 9pc.

stories.title: PTI asks govt to ‘rebuild trust’ if it is serious about talks
summary: Mr Akram demanded the reversal of measures the party considered unlawful, restoration of its provincial government’s mandate and release of political prisoners whose continued detention, he said, could not be legally justified.

Mr Akram said the government’s use of “coercive measures and political pressure” had failed to diminish the PTI’s public support.

stories.title: Balochistan lawyers go on strike over ANP leader’s arrest
summary: QUETTA: Awami Nat­ional Party’s Balochistan president was arrested on Wednesday after a court cancelled his bail in a road accident case.
The counsel for Asghar Khan Achakzai said the father of deceased Zahir Shah had lodged an FIR in Chaman police station accusing him of the fatal accident.
He stated, “Asghar Khan Achakzai has nothing to do with this case and he is like his brother.” When the case came up for hearing on Wednesday, the court cancelled the ANP leader’s bail.

stories.title: 10 killed, 44 injured as passenger bus overturns on highway in Punjab's Rajanpur
summary: DERA GHAZI KHAN: Ten people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil, Rescue 1122 said.

stories.title: Senate panel orders fresh MDCAT probe
summary: The Senate Standing Committee on National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination has directed the health ministry to conduct a fresh inquiry into complaints regarding the MDCAT 2026 examination within one week.
PMDC officials informed the committee that no irregularities or anomalies had been found during the examination.
The committee also expressed concern over the PMDC's practice of collecting question booklets from candidates after the examination and not allowing them to retain copies.

stories.title: Khyber takes over as commander Pakistan fleet
summary: Rear Admiral Khyber Zaman assumed the command as Commander Pakistan Fleet during Change of Command ceremony held at Fleet Headquarters, Karachi.

Rear Admiral Khyber Zaman is a graduate of Air War College (Karachi), National Defence University (Islamabad) and Naval Postgraduate College (USA), said a news release of Director General Public Relations (Navy).
His key appointments include Commander Field and Operational Sea Training (COMFOST), Naval Secretary and Additional Secretary-III at Ministry of Defence.

stories.title: Government websites go dark after AI-discovered flaw sparks security scramble
summary: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems.

stories.title: LHC moved for release of Imran's sisters as 30-day detention period ends
summary: LAHORE: The son of Aleema Khan, detained sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, moved the Lahore High Court (LHC) on Wednesday, seeking the production and release of his mother, as well as two aunts.
Aleema’s son, Shahrez Khan, filed a fresh plea challenging their detention in the LHC on Wednesday.
The petition stated that Imran’s sisters remained at Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail despite the lapse of the 30-day period of their detention.

stories.title: Senate body summons ASF official over alleged mistreatment of passengers at airports
summary: Taking up a privilege motion moved by Senator Zehri concerning the alleged inappropriate conduct of ASF personnel, the committee reviewed the response received regarding an inquiry report that it had sought last month.

The committee had taken up the privilege motion by Senator Zehri in a previous meeting on Sept 11, regarding alleged misbehaviour by ASF officials during a check-in for Emirates flight EK-601 on July 24.

According to the motion, a copy of which is available with Dawn, Senator Butt alleged a breach of her privilege and that of the Senate and its standing committee arising out of the conduct of the vice chancellor in connection with proceedings relating to matters concerning PIFD.

stories.title: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in alleged CCD encounter
summary: The suspect accused of running over and fatally injuring a 14-year-old boy in Multan was killed in an alleged encounter with the Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur early on Wednesday, police said.
A Multan court on Tuesday granted police three-day physical remand of the suspect.
On Tuesday, police requested a 14-day physical remand of the suspect for investigation.

stories.title: 10% inflation splits rate call predictions

stories.title: 'Urdu AI model Buraq to keep data at home'
summary: The minister told a World Bank panel on digital government service delivery that the model, and the public compute capacity behind it, form the AI layer of a programme built on four foundations, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of IT on Wednesday.

On data, WASL, the national exchange layer of the Digital Public Infrastructure stack built under the World Bank-supported Digital Economy Enhancement Project, lets institutions share data with every transaction authenticated, encrypted and logged.
On safeguards, the National Data Governance Policy sets a single rulebook for classifying, sharing, protecting and publishing public data.

stories.title: Cash flow data could unlock SME financing
summary: Speaking at the launch of NEO BIZ, a digital banking service for SMEs, Mashreq Bank Pakistan CEO Muhammad Hamayun Sajjad said businesses often maintained bookkeeping records that banks did not consider reliable enough for lending decisions.
Digital-first banking models could help bridge this gap by creating verifiable records of business transactions, including sales, payments and collections.
However, digital records alone would not guarantee financing, as lenders would still need to assess profitability, liabilities and business risks.

stories.title: PHC orders provisional de-sealing of KP Assembly deputy speaker's official residence
summary: The counsel further said that under Section 20 of the KP Provincial Assembly Speaker and Deputy Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975, Bibi was entitled to a “fully furnished official residence” in Peshawar for her “entire tenure as the deputy speaker”.

The lawyer claimed that following the imposition of governor’s rule on Oct 11, police, “without any reason and justification”, raided Bibi’s official residence to “harass her and illegally and unlawfully arrest her”.

She requested the court to direct the relevant respondents, including the provincial government and the KP IG, to “immediately” de-seal the premises and restore the her lawful access and possession to the official residence.

stories.title: Suspect should not be deprived of bail in case of 'reasonable doubt' over involvement, SC rules
summary: ISLAMABAD: Taking exception to the prosecution’s shifting stance without realising the gravity of that conduct in a case regarding expired drugs, the Supreme Court has ruled that whenever reasonable doubt arises, a suspect should not be deprived of the benefit of bail.

Based on these sections, a two-judge SC bench on April 16 granted post-arrest bail to the petitioner on furnishing bail bonds to the tune of Rs100,000 with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court.

When the SC’s bail order was sent for compliance, it emerged that the prosecution modified the first information report (FIR) by replacing the original provisions with Sections 409, 471, 468, 467, 420, 109 of PPC, read with Section 5 (2) of the 1947 Prevention of Corruption Act.

stories.title: Apple will have limited iPhone Duo units available in stores on Friday
summary: Apple on Wednesday said it will have ‘limited’ numbers of its folding iPhone Duo phone available for walk-in customers when the device launches on Friday, after initial online orders sold out in minutes and pushed delivery times for some customers to January.

Other regions will only have iPhone Duo units available for customers who already bought them online, including mainland China, France, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the UAE, Apple said.
On the China-governed island of Macau, the iPhone Duo will be available for walk-in customers only, with limited inventory, Apple said.

stories.title: Electronic Arts to cut 400 jobs, shut down BioWare, cancel next 'Mass Effect' game
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) plans to lay off 400 employees, close its BioWare studio and cancel the next "Mass Effect" game, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.
The layoffs will affect 3% of the US video game publisher’s workforce, including 50 employees at BioWare, the studio behind the popular "Mass Effect" and "Dragon Age" franchises.
The restructuring follows EA’s $55 billion Saudi-led buyout in August, which took the company private and added $18 billion in debt.

stories.title: Punjab govt rejects allegations of CM-ordered CCD encounters after Multan incident suspect's death
summary: Also Read: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in CCD encounter Bokhari said an investigation had revealed that the Multan incident suspect was short-tempered and ill-mannered and had treated Abbas harshly.

Bokhari said cases involving organised crime were referred to the CCD rather than the regular police to ensure more effective investigation and prosecution and to meet all legal requirements for delivering justice.

Earlier today, it expressed concern over Abbas's killing and the subsequent death of the primary suspect in an alleged police encounter, calling for an independent and transparent investigation into the case.

stories.title: Pakistani who allegedly defrauded US Postal Service remanded in NCCIA Lahore's custody
summary: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Wednesday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) five-day physical remand of a suspect in an alleged Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage labels.

The NCCIA’s Lahore zone announced his arrest at a press conference a day ago, saying that the suspect operated a website to market and sell over 5m fake postage stamps over a period of more than three years.
The agency’s investigating officer told the court that the suspect had allegedly been operating a website, LabelsBank.com, since August 2023 to sell more than 5m counterfeit postage labels.

stories.title: ATC appoints state counsel for Imaan, Hadi in security breach case
summary: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Wednesday appointed a state counsel to cross-examine prosecution witnesses from the defence side in a security breach case against lawyers Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha.

He had shown up in the Islamabad district and sessions court during a November hearing instead of Advocate Shakeel Jatt, the state counsel who was initially appointed to represent the duo in the case.

Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president.

stories.title: JI announces third wave of anti-levy protests across country on Friday
summary: LAHORE: The Jamaat-i-Islami Pakistan (JI) announced on Wednesday that it will launch the third phase of its nationwide protest movement against the petroleum levy on Friday, with sit-ins planned in all districts across the country, according to a press release by the party.

Wednesday’s press release by JI said the new phase of demonstrations would begin on the instructions of party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, and that the party’s clear and firm demand remained the complete abolition of the petroleum levy.
On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

stories.title: Interior minister returns Rs5 million to Laiba Ejaz's family, updates on case progress
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Wednesday handed Rs5 million to the family of late student Laiba Ejaz during a visit to her residence to offer condolences and brief the family on progress in the case.
Laiba's father told The Express Tribune that the interior minister handed him Rs5 million recovered by the police from the primary suspect.
The interior minister informed Laiba's family about the progress made in the investigation of her case/ “The entire team worked day and night on the Laiba Ejaz case.
